data.body: The job grants only `contents: read` and `pull-requests: write`, but `ensure_review_label()` in `scripts/pr_status_labels.py` creates the repository's `needs-review` label via `POST /repos/{repo}/labels` whenever it doesn't already exist. GitHub's repository Labels endpoints (`GET`/`POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels...`) are gated by the Issues permission scope: applying or removing an existing label on an issue/PR number works with `pull-requests: write` (GitHub disambiguates by the target number), but creating the label definition itself needs `issues: write`. Since `needs-review` is a brand-new label that won't already exist in any consuming repository — including this one, per `docs/pr-status-labels.md`'s own 'This repository runs the workflow on its own pull requests' — the very first `opened`/`reopened`/`ready_for_review` run from a non-writer author will fail at label creation with `Resource not accessible by integration`, the job exits non-zero, and no status label is applied at all, defeating the feature's purpose. Add `issues: write` to the job permissions (and update the matching usage snippet/security-model text in `docs/pr-status-labels.md` and the `test_token_can_only_read_contents_and_write_pull_requests` assertion that currently forbids `issues: write`), or pre-create `needs-review` out of band and drop the auto-create path.
